```{r}
#---- Packages ----
library(readxl)

library(viridis)
library(WaverideR)
library(cowplot)
```




```{r}
df <- read.csv("/Users/silkemaus/Downloads/PhD/April26/cyclo_EGU/1408_1410.csv")
#colnames(df)

series <- data.frame(
  depth = df$Depth.comp..mcd...two.site.composite..Depth.CCS....,
  TiAl = df$Ti_Al,
  Age = df$Age_Ma
)
colnames(series) <- c("depth", "TiAl", "Age")

series <- subset(series, depth >= 50 & depth <= 240)
series_1 <- subset(series, depth >= 50 & depth <= 100)

series_2 <- subset(series, depth >= 100 & depth <= 150)

series_3 <- subset(series, depth >= 150 & depth <= 240)



range(series_3$Age)

```

total Depth Span: 190 m Age Span: 6.39796 Myr --> 6397.96 kyr

--> SR = 190m/6.39796 Myr = 29.6970 m/Myr --> 2.97 cm/kyr

series 1: SR = 50m/1.48482 Myr = 33.68 m/Myr = 3.368 cm/kyr
series 2: SR = 50m/1.58985 = 3.14 cm/kyr
series 3: SR = 90/3.32 = 2.71 cm/kyr



```{r}
plot(series$depth, series$TiAl,
     type = "l",
     xlab = "Depth (mcd)",
     ylab = "Ti/Al",
     main = "U1410- U1408 Ti/Al vs Depth")
grid()
```
```{r}
# interpolate

series_3_int <- linterp(series_3)
```

ASM braucht:
# 1. Frequenzen aus MTM (cycles/m)
freq_TiAl <- TiAl_mtm$Frequency
# 2. Rayleigh frequency (aus Periodogramm)
Rayleigh frequency: 0.04681648 
# 3. Nyquist frequency (aus Periodogramm)
Nyquist frequency: 25 
# 4. Orbital target frequencies (cycles/kyr)
mittleres Eozän
target_pre <- c(1/23, 1/21, 1/19)
target_ob <- c(1/41)
target_ecc <- c(1/125, 1/100, 1/95)
target_405 <- c(1/405)
# 5. Suchbereich für Sedimentationsrate

```{r}
freq_TiAl <- TiAl_mtm_1$Frequency
ray <- 0.04681648
nyq <- 25
target_pre <- c(1/23, 1/21, 1/19)
target_ob <- c(1/41)
target_ecc <- c(1/125, 1/100, 1/95)
target_405 <- c(1/405)
```

 
 run ASM separately for precession, obliquity and eccentricity

```{r}
# eccentricity asm_1 # doesn't make sense because there is only one significant peak --> better to estimate sedrate directly: SR = 11.37/100 = 11.37 cm/kyr
freq_sig_1_ecc <- c(0.08795778)
TiAl_asm_1_ecc <- asm(freq = freq_sig_1_ecc,
                    target = target_ecc,
                    rayleigh = 0.019992 ,
                    nyquist = 25,
                    fper = rep(0.3, length(target_ecc)),
                    numsed = 100,
                    sedmin = 3,
                    sedmax = 20,
                    iter = 500,
                    genplot = TRUE,
                    output = TRUE,
                    linLog = 1)
```

```{r}
# precession asm series 1
freq_sig_1_pre <- c(1.015513, 1.155445, 1.259395, 1.475292, 1.523269, 1.595234)
TiAl_asm_1_pre <- asm(freq = freq_sig_1_pre,
                    target = target_pre,
                    rayleigh = 0.019992,
                    nyquist = 25,
                    fper = rep(0.3, length(target_pre)),
                    numsed = 100,
                    sedmin = 3,
                    sedmax = 20,
                    iter = 500,
                    genplot = TRUE,
                    output = TRUE,
                    linLog = 1)
```

try etimeopt
- it is built for variable sedimentation rates,
- uses moving windows,
```{r}


etime <- eTimeOpt(
    series_int,
    win = 60,
    step = 5,
    sedmin = 1,
    sedmax = 6,
    numsed = 200,
    linLog = 1,
    fit = 1,
    fitModPwr = TRUE,
    detrend = TRUE,
    output = 1,
    genplot = TRUE,
    check = TRUE,
    verbose = 1
)
```
